Welcome! This guide is here to help you get the most out of SOGo Groupware — your open-source collaboration platform for email, calendars, contacts, and more. Whether you are setting up your SOGo 5 account for the first time or looking to master advanced features like shared calendars, Sieve mail filters, or resource booking, you have come to the right place. Every tutorial in this guide is built from real, step-by-step screen captures — so you see exactly what to click, type, and expect at each step. No guesswork, no vague instructions.

SOGo supports high contrast and dark mode. Toggle via user preferences or use browser/OS-level accessibility settings: Windows: Win+Ctrl+C toggles high contrast macOS: System Preferences → Accessibility → Display → Increase contrast Browser Extensions: Dark Reader, High Contrast (Chrome) Orientation: if you lose your place, press Ctrl+Home (German keyboards: Strg+Pos1) to return to the top of the page and navigate from there.

This tutorial walks you through creating a new event in SOGo 5's calendar, including setting the date and time, adding attendees, and configuring reminders.
A SOGo 5 account with valid credentials You are logged into SOGo 5

In the sidebar navigation on the left, click Calendar to open the calendar view. The calendar opens in Week view by default. You can switch between Day, Week, Month, and Year views using the buttons in the top toolbar.

There are three ways to create an event: Method Action Click the + button Click the + (plus) button in the top toolbar Double-click Double-click on any time slot in the calendar grid Use the date picker Click a date in the mini-calendar on the left, then click + Choose whichever method you prefer. A new event dialog will appear.

Fill in the event details: Field Description Example Title A short name for your event "Team Standup" Location Where the event takes place "Conference Room B" Start Date and time the event begins Today at 10:00 End Date and time the event ends Today at 11:00 Calendar Which calendar to save to — chosen from your calendar list your account abbreviation Category A color-coded category Meeting (blue) tip For all-day events (e.g., birthdays, holidays), toggle the All-day switch. The time fields will be disabled.

If you want to invite other people: Click the Attendees section to expand it Start typing a colleague's name or email address Select the person from the auto-complete suggestions Choose their participation role: Required — Must attend Optional — Welcome but not required Repeat for each additional attendee SOGo 5 will send an email invitation to each attendee when you save the event.

To receive a reminder before the event: Click the Alarm section to expand it Choose when to be reminded: 15 minutes before (default) 30 minutes before 1 hour before 1 day before Custom — enter your own time Choose the reminder method: Display — A popup notification appears in your browser when the reminder fires Email — An email sent to your address. Note: Email alarms require the server-side sogo-ealarms-notify service — contact your administrator if email reminders never arrive You can combine multiple alarms per event (e.g., 15 minutes before as a popup plus 1 day before as an email): click Add alarm to do so
Use the Description field to add notes, an agenda, or preparation instructions for the event. This field supports plain text.

For events that repeat, click the Repeat section and choose a pattern: Pattern Example Daily Standup meeting every day Weekly Team meeting every Tuesday Bi-weekly Sprint review every two weeks Monthly Department meeting first Monday of each month Yearly Birthday or anniversary You can also set an end date for the recurrence (e.g., repeat until the end of the semester).

Click Save or OK (depending on your SOGo 5 version) to create the event. The event will appear on your calendar. If you added attendees, they will receive an email invitation that they can accept or decline.

You have successfully created a calendar event. You can now: Share your calendar with others Edit the event by clicking on it Drag and drop to reschedule Resize the event by dragging its edges to change duration

Check when your colleagues are available before scheduling a meeting — directly from the event creation dialog.

Free/busy data is not public. The grid can only show availability that each attendee has actively shared — which is why sharing has to go both ways: You see colleagues only if they shared with you. A calendar without granted access renders as "No data" — their availability stays invisible. Colleagues see you only if you shared with them. The same check runs in reverse when someone else schedules the meeting. One-way sharing breaks the workflow. If only one side shares, every lookup in the other direction fails — the "Are you free at…?" emails come back exactly where free/busy was supposed to end them. Before relying on the grid, make sharing mutual — once: Share your own calendar — at minimum free/busy permission for your team Ask attendees to do the same That is why "No data" is not an error: it is the permission system working as intended.

Open the Calendar module Click + to create a new event, or click an existing event to edit

In the event dialog, click the Attendees section Start typing a colleague's name or email address Select the person from the auto-complete list Repeat for each person you want to check Once attendees are entered, the free/busy grid opens automatically — there is no separate Free/Busy button.

The grid shows time slots for each person. Don't rely on color names — the exact colors depend on your SOGo skin and theme; read the status labels instead: Status Meaning Busy The colleague has an event Tentative Maybe attending Available Free at that time No entry / no data Calendar not shared with you, or outside working hours
Look for a time when all attendees show as available. SOGo 5 may suggest the next available slot automatically.
Click on the desired time slot in the grid. The event's start/end time updates to match.

What a colleague can see depends on two things: the rights they have on your calendar, and how each event is classified. 1. The rights they have on your calendar. When a calendar is shared, one of these rights is granted per person: Right What it allows See events without details Busy/free times only — no titles, no details See events with details Titles, times and descriptions Answer Respond to invitations Edit Create, change and delete events The free/busy view described in this guide is the "without details" view. 2. How each event is classified. Every event carries a visibility, set per event in the event dialog — Public, Private or Confidential. What someone actually sees for a given event depends on both: their right on the calendar and the event's classification. With "see without details" they only ever see busy blocks — regardless of classification.
Check they have a SOGo 5 account They may not have free/busy sharing enabled They might be in a different address book — try typing their full email

This is missing sharing, not a malfunction — see Why Calendar Sharing Must Be Mutual The colleague hasn't shared their calendar with you Ask the person or your administrator to grant you free/busy access

Free/busy lookup helps you find meeting times without the back-and-forth of "Are you free at...?" emails. It works for anyone in your organization who shares calendar availability. The one-time prerequisite is mutual sharing: the grid only shows calendars whose owners have granted access — in both directions.

Open the three-dot menu (⋯) next to the calendar again and select Sharing…: Change: adjust the person's permission Remove: delete the person's entry from the sharing list Save your change afterwards

Fill in the contact's details. The most commonly used fields are: Field Description Recommended First Name Given name ✅ Always Last Name Family name ✅ Always Email Primary email address ✅ Always Phone Telephone number Optional Mobile Mobile phone number Optional Organisation Organization or company Optional Role Function or role at the company Optional Title e.g., Dr., Prof. Optional tip The Display Name field is auto-filled from First + Last name, but you can customize it (e.g., "John D. If you have multiple address books, select which one to save to using the dropdown at the top of the contact form. Typically there is a personal address book — at the University of Marburg it carries your account abbreviation, like your Personal calendar — and possibly additional shared address books. Collected Addresses — Automatically saved from sent emails

Click Save to add the contact to your address book. The contact will now appear in your contact list. You can: Click on it to view or edit details Start typing the name when composing an email to auto-complete
In the top navigation, click + next to Lists Enter a name for the list (e.g., "Team", "Clients", "Family") Click OK
Drag a contact from the list onto the list name, or Click the three-dot menu (⋯) next to the list, select Add Members, and choose contacts

To import contacts from another service: Click the three-dot menu (⋯) in the contacts toolbar Select Import Choose a file: vCard (.vcf) — Standard format, works with most address books CSV (.csv) — Spreadsheet export format Click Import warning Imported contacts are added to the currently selected address book. Make sure the correct address book is selected before importing.
Edit: Click on a contact in the list, then click Edit Delete: Select the contact and click Delete (trash icon)

A SOGo 5 account with valid credentials You are logged into SOGo 5 At least two users with SOGo accounts (for delegation demonstration) Permissions managed per-folder or per-calendar

SOGo supports granular ACL-based permissions for: Resource Type What Can Be Shared Calendar Read-only, Full Control, Confidential availability Address Book Read, Write, Modify permissions Mail Folders View, Read, Post, Create, Delete access Categories Permission levels for event categorization

Permission Description Owner Full control, can change permissions Can Read View items only Can Edit Modify existing items Can Create Add new items Can Delete Remove items Reviewer Combination of read + approve/reject tip Use different permission levels based on trust level. For example, a colleague may get "Can Read" access to your calendar, while a delegated assistant may get "Can Edit" plus "Can Create."

In the module you want to share (Calendar or Contacts), click the three-dot menu (⋯) or Share button. info Not all modules in this test environment show the Share button. In a production setup with fully-permissive ACLs enabled, sharing options appear on individual items and collections.
The Share/Acl panel displays: Current owner Existing delegated users/groups Current permission level for each
Click Add or Share button Search for recipient by username, email address Select the target from search results
Choose the appropriate permission from the dropdown: Viewer (Markiert als Viewer) Participant (Markiert als Participant) Editor (Markiert als Editor) Administrator (Vollzugriff)
Toggle Send email notification if you want SOGo to email the recipient about the shared resource.
Click Apply or Save to activate the sharing.

Scenario Recommended Permission Why Assistant Administrator Needs full control to manage calendar on your behalf Team Lead Participant Can create/edit events to schedule team meetings Colleague Viewer Should see your availability without modifying Project Team Viewer (time-focused) Only needs to know when you're busy/free warning Changes to delegation permissions take effect immediately. Double-check permission levels before saving.

When a resource is shared to you: The shared resource appears in your module navigation (e.g., Calendar → Shared Calendars) Permission level determines what you can do: Viewer: Items appear fused or overlaid but are read-only Participant: Appears in your view, you can add/edit but deletions restricted Administrator: Full edit and delete access

Welcome! This page helps you get familiar with the SOGo 5 interface so you can start working right away.
Open your browser, enter your SOGo 5 instance URL (e.g. https://demo.sogo.nu/SOGo/), type your username and password, and click Login. After successful authentication you'll see the main dashboard.

Once logged in, the SOGo interface is divided into three main areas: Top navigation — Module navigation: click to switch between Mail, Calendar, Contacts, and Tasks. Top toolbar — Module tabs, the three-dot menu (⋯), and the logout power icon ⏻. Main content area — Where the active module's content is displayed.

Fill in the recipient fields: Field Description To Primary recipient(s). Separate multiple addresses with commas or semicolons Cc Carbon copy — recipients receive a copy, visible to others Bcc Blind carbon copy — recipients receive a copy, hidden from other recipients Tips: Start typing a name — SOGo 5 will suggest matching contacts from your address book You can also enter full email addresses directly Use Cc for people who need to be informed but are not directly responsible Use Bcc for mailing lists or when recipients should not see each other

Enter a clear, concise subject line in the Subject field. tip Good subject lines help recipients understand the purpose of your email. Examples: ❌ "Meeting" ✅ "Sprint Planning — Tuesday 10:00" ❌ "Question" ✅ "Question about calendar sharing permissions"

documents.t: SOGo 5 uses Sieve scripts for server-side mail filtering. Filters run when email arrives — before you see it in your inbox.
Click the three-dot menu (⋯) (Settings) in the top toolbar Select Mail → Filters
Click Create filter.

Choose when the filter should apply: Condition Example From contains @example.com → all mail from that domain Subject contains [Spam] → flag potential spam To contains team@company.com → mailing list messages Size larger than 5M → large attachments You can combine multiple conditions: All conditions must match (AND) Any condition can match (OR)

Choose what happens when conditions are met. Exact labels may vary slightly between versions — typical actions: Action Use Case Move to folder Sort into the right folder Copy to folder Keep a copy in inbox + file in folder Forward to Send to another address Mark as read Auto-archive newsletters Mark as flagged Highlight important senders Discard Delete spam (use with caution) Reject with message Bounce unwanted email with a custom message Important: Messages are only actually moved if you add Stop processing filter rules as the last action.
Filters run in order from top to bottom. Drag filters to reorder them. The first matching filter's action is applied.
Click Save or Apply. The Sieve script is compiled and activated on the server immediately.

Goal: Move all email from @company.com into the "Work" folder. Create the "Work" folder first (Part 1, Step 2) Open the filter settings → Create filter Condition: From contains @company.com Action: Move to folder → choose the "Work" folder Last action: Stop processing filter rules Click Save
Condition: Subject contains "URGENT" Action: Mark as flagged
Condition: From contains "newsletter@" Action: Move to folder "Newsletters"

Check that the filter's last action is Stop processing filter rules (see Step 4) Test with a simple filter first (e.g., move all mail from yourself) Whether Sieve is enabled (SOGoSieveScriptsEnabled = YES), which Sieve server address is configured, and whether server logs show Sieve compilation errors is part of the server configuration — that is your IT administration's job. Ask your administrator if in doubt.
Log out and log back in Check that the folder was created (not accidentally named with slashes)
Folders and filters help you maintain a clean inbox without manual effort. Start with 2–3 filters for your most common email patterns.

Reserve and schedule shared resources — meeting rooms, projectors, labs, or equipment — through SOGo's integrated calendar resource booking. info Resource booking in SOGo is typically implemented as special calendar accounts marked as resources. Your administrator configures these resource accounts, and they appear as available rooms or equipment when scheduling meetings.

Resource accounts are typically created with these attributes: Setting Value User Role Resource (not person) Location Physical address or room number Capacity Number of people that can be accommodated Equipment List Specific equipment available in resource note Setting up resources requires administrative access to SOGo automated scripts or direct database edits. Ask your admin if a resource you need is not available.

Book in advance — resources are shared; last-minute booking may fail. Provide details — in the event description, include meeting purpose, needed preparation, number of attendees. Be considerate — if you just need a few minutes, don't block for a full day if not necessary. Release when done — if you finish early or the meeting cancels, remove the event/booking. Avoid double-booking yourself — resource system checks conflicts for you, but be judicious.

The openEduSuite chat runs on Element — a chat built on the open Matrix network. From the portal tile, sign in with your openEduSuite account and you land directly in the messenger: rooms for courses, working groups, or one-to-one conversations, on any device.

The first time you sign in on a new device, Element asks you to verify your identity — the university's Element greets you in German ("Bestätige deine Identität"; in an English browser: "Confirm your identity"). This step sets up the encryption that protects your messages: Nimm ein anderes Gerät (use another device) — the recommended path if you already use Element elsewhere: the other device confirms the new one, and your message history stays intact. Bestätigung nicht möglich? (cannot verify?) — skips the verification, but with a price the app spells out before you continue: your account data, contacts, settings, and chat lists are kept, but message history stored only on the server is lost, and all devices and contacts must be verified again. Confirm with Fortfahren (continue) only if you have nothing to lose — on a fresh account, for example. After skipping, the wizard asks two quick confirmations: a single sign-on step ("use Single Sign-On to confirm your identity") and the encryption setup (Bestätigen — confirm). Each is one click; then Fertig (done) closes the dialog and the messenger is yours. If you use the chat seriously, verify properly on your second device the first chance you get — one honest minute beats a lost history.

Once inside, Element works like any modern messenger: rooms in the left column, the conversation on the right, and the composer at the bottom. Start rooms for your work, join the ones your courses and colleagues share, and keep an eye on your notifications. Element encrypts by design: what you write stays between you and your rooms — including from the server operators, once devices are verified. Opening a project leads to its workspace. The sidebar carries: New — starts a new session; the command palette calls it "Start a new research conversation". Search — the command palette. It searches sessions, transcript messages, workspace files, artifacts, and project actions, and gathers the app's actions in one list (from New session to Open settings and Open documentation). Customize — the settings (see below). The workspace actions Files, Terminal, Compute, and Autoresearch. Sessions — the project's session list, with a New session button. What the workspace actions show: Files — the project's files, with a More menu ("Add folder…", "Manage workspace folders…"). An empty folder says "This folder is empty". Terminal — commands inside the project; without a connection to the local OpenScience server it reports "Local terminal unavailable". Compute — the machine behind the project ("This computer"): active and running counts, memory, and CPU cores. Autoresearch — studies that hill-climb a metric, each with its score, its runs, and its queue. An empty project says "No studies yet" and suggests asking in a session for a study: the metric to improve, the budget, and the script to run.

Customize opens the Settings dialog with sections for Account, General, Workspaces, Models, Research, Skills, Tools, Connectors, Credentials, and System (compute, permissions, network, sandbox, storage). General holds the theme (System, Light, Dark) and the display language: OpenScience follows your browser's language, so with a German browser much of the interface appears in German ("Erscheinungsbild", "Hell" and "Dunkel", "Terminal umschalten") while the rest stays English. The Open documentation entry in the command palette leads to the project's README on GitHub.

EWOKS — reproducible, multi-step processing as a workflow; OpenScience's autoresearch studies instead hill-climb a single metric, run by run. Nextcloud and OpenCloud — plain file storage without compute sessions. A project is the unit: its sessions, files, and artifacts are all reachable from its command palette. Operaton is the workflow engine of the openEduSuite: administrative and collaborative processes run here digitally — approvals, applications, checklists. You meet it when a process assigns you a task.

After signing in from the portal, open the Tasklist. It shows the tasks assigned to you, for example under All tasks. Open a task to see its form: details, fields to fill in, and a button to complete the step — sometimes a choice between several paths. What you see exactly depends on the process. Some lists keep a filter so you see only what matters to you; the number next to a list entry shows how many tasks it currently holds. With no tasks waiting, the list says so plainly ("No task matching filters found.") — then there is simply nothing for you to do.

Many processes can also be started by you directly: choose Start process — a panel opens with the processes your university has deployed ("Click on the process to start"). Pick the process, fill in the form that follows, and submit it. The process then routes through the university's defined steps — you will meet it again as a task whenever your part is due. A process can set real things in motion — user accounts, virtual machines, invoices. Start only what you are responsible for. If the service stays closed to you, the helpdesk reaches its operators.

Overleaf is the LaTeX workbench of the openEduSuite — write papers, theses, and reports in LaTeX, compiled while you type, together in one project. The portal tile LaTeX (Overleaf) and the suite account open the Projects page directly; the instance answers as openEduSuite Overleaf (SSO).

The left menu sorts the work: Your projects, Shared with you, Archived projects, and Trash; under Organize tags, New tag collects projects, and the search field filters the list. The project list is a table — Title, Owner, Last modified — with per-row actions Copy, Download .zip file, Download PDF, Archive, and Trash. New project opens the menu: Blank project, an Existing project (.zip) import, or Templates with an Example project. You are asked for the Project name, then Create starts the project.

The editor splits three ways: the File tree — New file, New folder, Upload — with the File outline on the left, the LaTeX source in the middle, and the compiled PDF on the right. With Auto compile on (the default), the PDF rebuilds as you type; Recompile forces a build, and the compile menu adds Fast [draft] mode and Stop on first error. The menu bar (File, Edit, Insert, …) carries the LaTeX tools; the top bar opens Share and Chat for collaboration.

Typst — modern markup, instant preview, easier start; first choice for most people. Overleaf — LaTeX: journals, citation styles, and templates that already exist in .tex. First choice when the target venue speaks LaTeX. If the service stays closed to you, the helpdesk reaches its operators.

The portal is the entry point of the openEduSuite: your digital workplace. You can read it without signing in — it then shows the weather for Marburg, the university news, and the events calendar. The language selector in the top bar switches the portal between Deutsch, English, Français and 中文.

Choose Anmelden in the top bar (Login when the portal runs in English) and sign in with your openEduSuite account — the same login that works everywhere in the suite. See Signing In: One Login for All Apps for details. After signing in, the portal shows your personal digital workplace: the app tiles plus weather, news and events. The top bar now holds Konto (Account in English), which opens the account console in a new tab, and Abmelden (Logout), which signs you out.

The account console manages everything about your openEduSuite login: your profile, your password, two-factor authentication, and the devices you are signed in on. Open it from any signed-in app, or go to your account page directly and sign in when asked.
Shows your account details: Username and Email First name and Last name Your username and name are managed by your university; contact your helpdesk if something is wrong there.

Two sections control how you sign in: Basic authentication: choose Update to change your password Two-factor authentication: choose Set up Authenticator application to add a second factor Two-factor authentication pairs your login with an authenticator app on your phone: after entering your password, you also type a code from the app. We recommend setting it up — it protects your account even if someone learns your password.

Lists the devices and browsers where you are signed in. For each entry you can choose Sign out to end that single session, or Sign out all devices to end every session at once. Use it when you finish working on a shared computer, or when you want to be safe after using a device you do not control.

The openEduSuite's writing studio is built around Typst — the modern typesetting engine that turns plain text into polished PDFs, without LaTeX's steep edges. In the browser you write, the preview builds itself live, and the PDF export is one click.

From the portal tile, sign in with your openEduSuite account — single sign-on takes you straight to your Projects page. It lists your papers with owner and last-edited date, each with Open, Rename, Copy, and Archive actions, and switches between Active and Archived. The navigation offers Gallery, Profile, and Tasks alongside, plus Help — a help center with guides on getting started, editing and preview, packages, and LaTeX projects.

Create Project opens the small form: give your paper a Project name, pick Typst as the project type (LaTeX sits next to it), and Create opens the editor. Browse templates leads to the gallery of maintained starting points. The editor carries the tabs View, Files, Preview, Settings, and Revisions; source text on one side, the rendered preview on the other. Typst's markup is lighter than LaTeX: = headings, - lists, $…$ math. When the paper is ready, the preview panel's Download PDF button exports it.

Fast feedback — the preview follows your typing, not a compiler Gentle syntax — readable source that still typesets tables, figures, math, and bibliographies In the browser — nothing to install; your projects wait in the studio wherever you sign in For longer documents that outgrow a chat or the wiki, the studio is the place — and finished PDFs fit right into your cloud files. The openEduSuite wiki is the shared knowledge base: documentation, how-tos, and course material that belongs together — written by everyone, for everyone. It runs on XWiki, one of the longest-lived open wiki engines.

The wiki is openly readable — no account is needed to browse. In the top bar, Log-in sits next to Register — reached from the portal tile. Choose Log-in: you are passed to the openEduSuite sign-in, and back into the wiki with your name attached to what you change.

The wiki's main page is its front door: a Welcome to your wiki heading with the first sections — The basics, Extend your wiki and Create your application — and pointers to extend the wiki. The basics tells you to log in and then use the Edit button above this page, the Create button above to add more pages, and the breadcrumbs above the title to navigate. It also points to a Sandbox — a place meant for experimenting with the wiki's features. The action bar keeps Edit, Create and More Actions ready.

A wiki grows by small steps: click Edit, improve what is there, and save with a short note in the Version summary field on what changed. Create starts a new page. Want to practice first? The main page's The basics section points to the Sandbox as a place to experiment. Every change is kept: open More Actions and choose History — it lists all revisions of a page, with Rollback available. The same menu groups Copy under Manage, Export and Print Preview under Actions, and Source, Children, Comments, Attachments and Information under Viewers. For team material that changes often, the wiki beats file attachments — and it links naturally with your projects and conversations in the chat.

Next to the main wiki there is a second instance for staff material: xwiki-staff.openedusuite.org. It works the same way: openly readable, and Log-in passes you to the openEduSuite sign-in with your suite account. Use the staff wiki for internal staff material, and the main wiki for content that is meant for everyone. If the service stays closed to you, the helpdesk reaches its operators.
